hero_headline: Democrats Sweep Both Chambers; Markets Bet on Slower AI Spending, Tariff Relief and an Iran Reset
daily_overview: Democrats won control of both chambers of Congress, and the aftershocks are already moving markets and diplomacy. US tech shares rallied on the view that divided government will slow the AI capital-spending race, while alcohol and consumer stocks jumped on hopes for tariff and immigration relief. Canada sees a path back to trade talks; Tehran and Moscow read the result as a vote against war. In technology, OpenAI agreed to buy Pierre Computer Company to deepen Codex's code-review tools, Anthropic published research on provable inference, and DeepMind showed agentic cheminformatics workflows proposing novel compounds. Finance had its own reversals: CVS plans to spin off roughly 9,000 drugstores, Sequoia is closing its London office, Solvay signed a Brazilian rare-earths deal to reduce reliance on China, and Canva is cutting more than 1,000 roles. The connecting thread is verification and cost: who audits an agent's output, and who pays for the compute behind it.

tech_briefs.title: OpenAI to Acquire Pierre Computer Company to Expand Codex's Code-Review Tooling
tech_briefs.summary: OpenAI said it will acquire Pierre Computer Company, folding the startup's tools into Codex for building, understanding and reviewing code. The deal extends OpenAI's push to make its coding assistant a full software-development environment rather than a completion engine, competing with rivals that already bundle review, testing and repository-level context.

tech_briefs.title: Anthropic Publishes Research on Provable Inference for Large Language Models
tech_briefs.summary: Anthropic outlined progress toward provable inference, an approach that aims to give mathematical or cryptographic guarantees about which weights and computations produced a given output. The work drew attention on Hacker News as enterprises and regulators seek verifiable assurances for agents handling money, code and sensitive data, rather than relying on vendor claims.

tech_briefs.title: Google DeepMind Applies Agentic Workflows to Cheminformatics With Antigravity
tech_briefs.summary: DeepMind described how Google Antigravity and its Cheminformatics Skills speed up drug-discovery workflows, searching compound libraries and proposing novel rigidified macrocycles. The post illustrates the shift from chat-style assistants to tool-using agents that run domain-specific scientific pipelines, a direction several labs now argue is the fastest route to measurable research productivity gains.

tech_briefs.title: NVIDIA's Auto-Ontology Builds a Semantic Graph Layer Beneath LLM Reasoning
tech_briefs.summary: Auto-Ontology is a Python framework that places a semantic, graph-based reasoning layer over existing data, allowing deterministic query generation and explainable context retrieval instead of fuzzy vector matching. That matters because agent failures often trace to schema confusion; an explicit ontology constrains what a model may assert and makes outputs auditable. It signals NVIDIA's interest in the reasoning scaffolding around models, not just the hardware beneath them.

tech_briefs.title: Worktrunk Offers a CLI for Managing Git Worktrees Across Parallel AI Agents
tech_briefs.summary: Worktrunk is a command-line tool for managing Git worktrees, letting several AI coding agents work in isolated checkouts of one repository without branch collisions or constant stashing. It addresses a practical bottleneck in concurrent agent workflows, where multiple editors touch the same codebase at once. Small projects like this show developer tooling being reshaped around agent-driven parallel sessions.

finance_briefs.title: US Stocks Rally After Democratic Sweep as Traders Bet on Slower AI Spending and Tariff Relief
finance_briefs.summary: US technology shares led the market higher on bets that a Democrat-controlled Congress will temper the scale of AI capital spending, while alcohol and consumer names jumped on hopes for a softer trade and immigration stance. Investors framed the midterm result as a check on policies that have driven both chip demand and import costs. (multiple reports)

finance_briefs.title: CVS Health to Break Up $102bn Empire With Spin-Off of Roughly 9,000 Drugstores
finance_briefs.summary: CVS Health plans to separate its pharmacy business, spinning off about 9,000 stores, as political pressure intensifies on pharmacy benefit managers and health insurers. The breakup would reverse years of vertical integration and hand investors two simpler businesses, though questions remain over debt allocation and the profitability of the remaining retail footprint.

finance_briefs.title: Sequoia Shuts London Office as Firm Refocuses on Silicon Valley
finance_briefs.summary: Sequoia is closing its London office, a retreat by one of the highest-profile tech investors and a setback to UK ambitions of becoming a leading AI hub. The move concentrates decision-making in Silicon Valley at a moment when European founders already complain about a funding gap for late-stage rounds.

finance_briefs.title: Solvay Signs Rare-Earths Deal to Supply Magnets From a Brazilian Mine
finance_briefs.summary: Solvay struck a rare-earths supply agreement drawing on a Brazilian mine, aimed at bolstering high-tech magnet production in Europe and the US and reducing dependence on Chinese processing. The deal is one of several Western efforts to build non-Chinese supply chains for materials used in motors, wind turbines and defense hardware.

finance_briefs.title: Canva Cuts More Than 1,000 Roles After What Its CEO Called Its Hardest Year
finance_briefs.summary: Canva chief executive Melanie Perkins said more than 1,000 staff will lose their jobs or be asked to change roles, describing the past year as the company's hardest. The cuts show design and productivity software vendors restructuring even while marketing AI features heavily, with headcount shifting toward engineering and AI product work.

politics_briefs.title: Foreign Capitals Read the Democratic Sweep as a Signal on Tariffs, Oil and the Iran War
politics_briefs.summary: From Kyiv to Moscow and Tehran to Tel Aviv, governments weighed how a flipped Congress changes US foreign policy. Canada saw a path to tariff relief with trade talks back on, Iranian officials called the result a vote against war, and commentators tied the outcome to oil prices and the conflict with Iran. (multiple reports)

politics_briefs.title: Ukraine Says Russian Double-Tap Strike Killed at Least 40 in Zaporizhzhia Village
politics_briefs.summary: Kyiv said bodycam footage shows a Russian double-tap attack on Komyshuvakha in the Zaporizhzhia region, with at least 40 confirmed dead and about 30 possibly still under rubble. President Zelenskyy called the strike on a school insane, while the Kremlin said it hopes the US midterms do not affect talks. (multiple reports)

politics_briefs.title: More Iranian Officials Argue for Building a Nuclear Weapon After War With US
politics_briefs.summary: Some Iranian clerics and officials are publicly arguing that Tehran should abandon its longstanding pledge not to build a nuclear bomb and rebuild deterrence after the war with the United States. The shift in rhetoric complicates any future negotiations and gives European capitals a reason to press for revived inspections.

editor_note: Today's brief leans on the US midterms because the result touches almost everything else: AI capital spending, tariffs, energy permitting and the Iran conflict. Tech items appear where they change how agents are built or verified, not merely where they are announced. Figures are as reported by the cited outlets.
